issues.failure_explanation: The proof correctly derives the displayed inequality, but the left-hand side involves E_n = Theta_n - R_n, where R_n accumulates the positive parts of delta_{j,k} = b_{j,k+1} - b_{j-1,k} over all j<=n. For variable order the coefficient of ||phi^k||^2 in E_n is b_{n,k} - sum_{j=k+1}^n (delta_{j,k})_+; b_{n,k} = O(tau) while sum_j (delta_{j,k})_+ is a sum of order-differences F_m(nu_j)-F_m(nu_{j-1}) of terms whose total is O(1). For an admissible continuous nu(t) oscillating between two values at the scale of tau (allowed by Assumption orders_bounds, which only requires continuity), the positive parts do not cancel and E_n is strongly negative, so the inequality E_n + (positive terms) <= C gives no bound on the discrete solution at all. Even for Lipschitz nu, positivity requires a smallness condition (roughly L*T bounded) that is never stated. Nothing in the paper shows E_n >= 0, let alone E_n >= c||phi^n||^2 (and Theta_n itself only controls b_{n,n}||phi^n||^2 = O(tau^{1-nu})||phi^n||^2), so the result titled 'Stability' and the contribution claim 'we establish stability' are not supported.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either prove a coercivity lemma E_n >= c Theta_n (or E_n >= 0) under an added regularity/smallness assumption on nu (e.g. Lipschitz with L T small), or replace the E-based argument by Lemma lem:frac1 combined with the discrete fractional Grönwall theorem (as in the convergence proof) to obtain a genuine bound on ||u_h^n||^2 + ||B_h^n||^2 and the dissipation sums.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem thm:stability does not establish boundedness of the fully discrete velocity/magnetic field or even of the dissipation sums for general admissible order functions; the prose claims of stability (abstract, contribution (3), Section 2.3 remark on non-monotone orders) are unsupported. The convergence theorem is unaffected because it uses Lemma lem:frac1 instead.
issues.title: Stability theorem bounds a corrected memory functional that is never shown to be nonnegative or coercive; the estimate can be vacuous
issues.why_classification: A genuine stability estimate can be recovered with a contained replacement argument already available in the paper (Lemma lem:frac1 plus Theorem 3.2 of Liao), or with a new coercivity lemma under an added hypothesis; no global architecture change, but a new lemma or restructured proof is required and the current statement carries no stability content.

In the periodic case, the corresponding estimate is

In the periodic case, we additionally assume that the velocity and magnetic field have zero spatial mean.

issues.failure_explanation: In the periodic case the discrete spaces V_h, C_h are conforming subspaces of H^1_per, which contain constants; for a constant v_h the right-hand side ||grad v_h|| vanishes while ||v_h|| does not, so the stated Poincaré inequality (and the Ladyzhenskaya inequality relying on zero mean) is false 'for all v_h in V_h'. Zero mean is assumed only for the exact solution, not for the discrete solution u_h^n, B_h^n, nor for the error xi_u^n = Pi_h u^n - u_h^n, nor for f, g. The stability proof (bounding <f^n,u_h^n> by ||f||_{H^{-1}} ||grad u_h^n||) and the convergence proof (Poincaré/Ladyzhenskaya for xi) therefore invoke an inequality outside its hypotheses in the periodic case.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: In the periodic case define V_h, C_h (and the projectors) as zero-mean subspaces and assume f^n, g^n and the discrete initial data have zero spatial mean, so that (testing with constants) the discrete solutions and errors remain mean-free and the Poincaré/Ladyzhenskaya inequalities apply.
issues.overall_effect: Theorems thm:stability and thm:convergence are not established as stated for periodic boundary conditions; only the Dirichlet case is covered by the given arguments.
issues.title: Poincaré and Ladyzhenskaya inequalities asserted for all discrete functions in the periodic case, although zero mean is not enforced
issues.why_classification: Adding the standard zero-mean setting for the discrete spaces and data restores every claim, rate and regime with a short local modification and no new argument.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof absorbs ||r_1^n||^2 + ||r_2^n||^2 into C tau^2, i.e. it uses ||^C D^{alpha(t_n)} u(t_n) - Delta_tau^{alpha(t_n)} u^n|| <= C tau uniformly. The L1 truncation estimate (O(tau^{2-nu}) <= O(tau)) requires a bound on the second time derivative of the solution in L^2(Omega); Assumption assu:regularity only provides partial_t u, partial_t B in L^infty(H^{l+1}) and no control of partial_tt u, partial_tt B. With merely bounded first derivatives the L1 error need not be O(tau). Hence the tau-rate in the theorem rests on an unstated hypothesis.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the assumption partial_tt u, partial_tt B in L^infty(0,T;L^2(Omega)^2) (or C^2 in time) to Assumption assu:regularity, which yields ||r_i^n|| <= C tau^{2-alpha^*} <= C tau for the fixed-order-per-level L1 formula.
issues.overall_effect: The temporal rate O(tau) in Theorem thm:convergence is unsupported under the stated assumptions; the theorem's hypotheses are incomplete.
issues.title: O(tau) truncation error of the variable-order L1 formula is used without any assumption on second time derivatives
issues.why_classification: A standard additional regularity hypothesis restores the stated rate and scope without changing the argument.

issues.failure_explanation: Subtracting (eq:fully_u1) from (eq:semi_u1) and testing with xi_u^n produces the terms (1/Re)(grad psi_u^n, grad xi_u^n) - (psi_p^n, div xi_u^n). The Stokes projector is defined without the factor 1/Re, so it only gives (grad psi_u, grad xi_u) = (psi_p, div xi_u); the residual (1/Re - 1)(grad psi_u^n, grad xi_u^n) does not vanish for Re != 1, yet no such term appears in (eq:conv_step2). The error identity as written is therefore incorrect for general Re (the numerical tests use Re = 200, 300).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define the Stokes projector with the weight 1/Re (or add the term (1/Re - 1)(grad psi_u^n, grad xi_u^n) to (eq:conv_step2) and bound it by epsilon/Re ||grad xi_u^n||^2 + C_epsilon ||grad psi_u^n||^2, absorbing it into I_2).
issues.overall_effect: The derivation of (eq:conv_step2) and hence of (eq:conv_step5) is incomplete for Re != 1; the final rate is unaffected once the term is included, since it is bounded by epsilon||grad xi_u||^2 + C h^{2l}.
issues.title: Error equation omits the diffusion/pressure projection term caused by the unscaled Stokes projector when Re != 1
issues.why_classification: A short local correction (rescaling the projector or adding one routine Young estimate) preserves the statement, rate and scope.
